Subject: SOC 2 Type II applicability across hosting modes

Hi Jordan,

Quick one from our InfoSec team as we prepare for our vendor assessment: can you confirm which Redwood hosting modes are covered by your most recent SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2027-09-30)? Specifically AtlasBank needs to know whether: 

- Requests through the public Redwood API (hosted) are in-scope for your Type II report,
- Dedicated/reserved pools (we plan to request a pinned pool for our tenant) are covered or require a bridge letter, and
- Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are covered or excluded.

Attached is our brief SIG/CAIQ extract and a short list of required evidence items (AtlasBank_SIG_Q3-2027.xlsx). Could you please indicate:
1) Which modes are explicitly covered by the Type II report,
2) If a bridge letter is available for dedicated pools or hosted-to-dedicated transitions, and
3) A short list of the evidence you can provide (SOC report, bridge letter, tenant mapping, network diagram) and an estimated delivery timeline.

We have an internal deadline of Nov 12 for procurement sign-off. Appreciate a quick confirmation — even a short note to confirm what's in/out will keep things moving.

Thanks,

Arielle Morris
Vendor Risk Manager | AtlasBank

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II applicability across hosting modes

Hi Arielle — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping in Kimberly from Compliance to give the authoritative answer, but to set expectations quickly:

- Hosted (public Redwood API): typically in-scope when you call our hosted endpoints; covered by the Type II for the reported period.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): can be in-scope if the dedicated pool is account/tenant-pinned and the tenancy isolation is operated as a Redwood-managed pool during the audit period — otherwise covered via a bridge letter or attestation.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: generally out-of-scope for Redwood's hosted SOC 2 Type II; customers often provide their own evidence or request a vendor attestation.

Kimberly, can you confirm the wording we should provide (bridge letter availability, specific evidence artifacts, and a realistic timeline to get a signed bridge template and tenant mapping)? Arielle — if you can share the tenant mapping file (or confirm how you'll identify the endpoints tied to AtlasBank) that will speed things up.

Jordan Blake

Hi Arielle — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. I wanted to provide a concise, auditable breakdown and the next steps so AtlasBank procurement can proceed with clarity.

Summary (short):
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted endpoints): INCLUDED in Redwood's SOC 2 Type II covering the period ending 2027-09-30. The report covers our hosted control environment and production clusters that service multi-tenant API requests. Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report PDF (control descriptions + test results), network diagram for hosted topology, and sampling logs.

2) Dedicated / Reserved Pools: CONDITIONALLY INCLUDED. If AtlasBank is on a dedicated pool that was allocated and operational under Redwood management for the audited period and tenant routing was pinned (no cross-tenant sharing in that pool), then the dedicated pool is eligible for inclusion. If the dedicated capacity was provisioned after the audit end date or if routing is cross-pooled, we provide a bridge letter that documents the controls equivalence for the dedicated pool and rolling-forward coverage. Evidence we can provide: tenant-to-pool mapping (CSV), pool provisioning timestamps, configuration snapshots, and a signed bridge letter templated from our compliance team.

3) Private / VPC / On-prem: EXCLUDED from Redwood's hosted SOC 2 Type II. For VPC/private deployments we can provide a supplier attestation and the SOC 2 control mapping we recommend customers use for their internal audits. We can also coordinate a point-in-time evidence package (network config, KMS integration logs) where feasible.

Requested evidence items (what we'll provide):
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) for period 2027-04-01 to 2027-09-30
- Draft bridge letter (redwood_bridge_template.docx) with space for customer & pool identifiers
- Tenant-to-pool mapping (tenant_mapping.csv) showing the AtlasBank tenant ID and assigned pool(s) during the period
- Hosted topology network diagram (PNG/PDF)
- Sampling logs and token-level routing trace excerpts (redacted)

Timeline:
- SOC 2 report (PDF): available now — will deliver upon NDA acknowledgement (we can send encrypted link) — target: 24 hours
- Draft bridge letter: 2 business days to populate and circulate for signatures (DocuSign link provided)
- Tenant mapping & config snapshots: dependent on your consent to share tenant identifiers; once we receive identifiers, we can produce CSV and timestamps within 48 hours.

For procurement: please confirm 1) whether AtlasBank will require a signed bridge letter for Dedicated pools, and 2) the tenant identifier(s) we should use to extract mapping. If you prefer, Grace O'Connor (copied) can host a short call to walk through the artifacts and the DocuSign flow.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
